question: A patient with CKD has a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) of 180 mg/g on two consecutive samples. According to KDIGO 2012, this falls into which albuminuria category?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A1 is ACR <30 mg/g (includes the normal range <10 and microalbuminuria 10–29).
Correct. A2 is ACR 30–300 mg/g (moderately increased, formerly 'microalbuminuria'). ACR 180 mg/g falls squarely in A2.
Incorrect. A3 is ACR >300 mg/g (severely increased, formerly 'macroalbuminuria' or proteinuria).

answers.text: Cannot be staged without a 24-hour urine protein

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. KDIGO 2012 uses the spot urine ACR (albumin-to-creatinine ratio) as the preferred method for albuminuria staging — a 24-hour collection is not required.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review KDIGO A-staging. ACR 180 mg/g = A2 (30–300 mg/g). The three categories are A1 <30, A2 30–300, A3 >300 mg/g.
Correct. KDIGO albuminuria categories: A1 <30 mg/g, A2 30–300 mg/g, A3 >300 mg/g. ACR 180 mg/g = A2. Combined G/A staging drives risk stratification and monitoring frequency.
